qa.answer: Five options. Reroute the fan cowl panels by truck to AMS and fly (USD 4.8K, no slip, recommended), reroute both the panels and the compound via AMS (USD 9.6K, no slip), wait for the next rotation (USD 12K of LDs, Kestrel Bay moves 2 days), split all three via DOH (about USD 18.6K, oversize ULD transfer risk), or induct on time and fit the panels last (no cost if the panels are off the critical path for the first 3 days).

Re-sequencing WO-2607 costs nothing, but it only works if planning confirms the cowl panel fit can wait until 15 Oct without consuming the single day of float. The cheapest option with no planning risk is the recommended AMS reroute at USD 4.8K, which the forwarder has already quoted.

In 2022 freighter capacity out of FRA collapsed for three weeks and six nacelle and chemical shipments were stuck at the gateway (PRE-01). We trucked them to AMS and flew from there for USD 21.4K; all six landed within 2 days of plan and no induction moved. The lesson was to pre-agree an AMS fallback rate with the forwarder so the reroute is a one-click booking.

WO-2607 inducts into Nacelle cell N-02 on 12 Oct and needs three fan cowl panels from Halvorsen on SHP-880436. The suspended rotation moves their arrival from 9 Oct to 15 Oct, a 3 day slip against 1 day of float, so the Kestrel Bay Cargo redelivery moves from 11 Nov to 13 Nov. WO-2624 slips 2 days inside 4 days of float and the WO-2623 forgings arrive well before the 30 Oct induction.
